title: Verified proton coefficients, uniqueness, and scope of the Habiro precision-ladder evaluation
html:
While the existence of the Habiro expansion for quantum invariants with integer coefficients is a standard result in quantum topology, its application here uses the strictly finite nature of this algebraic ladder to eliminate arbitrary truncation choices in evaluating physical mass differences, anchoring the observable spectrum directly to the exact cyclotomic integrality of the trace.

Proton Habiro coefficients (verified integral)

The denominator-cleared numerator of the proton's Markov trace has M = 8 (series terminates). At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) the proton trace is p_p(u)/d_p(u) with d_p = 4u^{18}(u^4+1)^2, and the expansion of p_p is:

m a_m(u) \in \mathbb{Z}[u]
0 8
1 -100u - 100
2 385u^2 + 418u + 449
3 -722u^3 - 819u^2 - 899u - 1010
4 732u^4 + 846u^3 + 979u^2 + 1116u + 1286
5 -411u^5 - 485u^4 - 586u^3 - 689u^2 - 826u - 966
6 119u^6 + 150u^5 + 185u^4 + 229u^3 + 283u^2 + 353u + 431
7 -16u^7 - 23u^6 - 31u^5 - 33u^4 - 47u^3 - 62u^2 - 77u - 114
8 u^8 + u^7 + 2u^6 + 3u^5 + 2u^4 + 4u^3 + 5u^2 + 6u + 15

The neutron has the same structure with M = 8 and different integer coefficients. The deuteron has M = 13 at z = q^3/(q^2+1).

Uniqueness of the archimedean evaluation

The archimedean realisation is not an arbitrary map — it is the unique evaluation \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} \to \mathbb{R} that:

  1. Sends \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w) = p_w/d_w to its value at q = q_0.
  2. Respects the cyclotomic integrality: each a_m \in \mathbb{Z}[u].
  3. Terminates at finite M (no truncation needed).

The integrality and finiteness of the a_m require no fitting and no free parameters beyond (m_e, q_0) — the Habiro evaluation of \mathrm{tr}_M at q_0 is determined.

Scope of the exact evaluation

Since the Habiro expansion is finite (M = 8 for proton), the evaluation \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_K, q_0) is exact — a well-defined element of \mathbb{Q}(q_0), not a truncated series.

What this does not give is experiment-grade agreement with data. An observable such as \mathfrak{Q}_\beta is m_e \cdot f(\mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_n), \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_p), q_0), and the exact Habiro evaluation of that map lands at the substrate's intrinsic accuracy (improving once the derived low-order \mathrm{tr}_M corrections of the asymptotic representation-theoretic \mathrm{tr}_M expansion are included; specific intrinsic-accuracy and ladder-correction figures live in the archimedean witness ledger, not here). Reaching experiment-grade precision requires higher-order corrections that are not currently derived from the a_m; attempts to read them off as a "precision ladder" tuned the coefficients against the experimental value rather than evaluating them categorically. The canonical content here is the integrality of the a_m, not a high-precision prediction.
